title: Continuous-startup thermal kernel: measured Krško transient
conclusion: The shared production thermal kernel was compared with measured operating-plant data. Missing event-era inputs and model limitations prevent physical acceptance; all discrepancies remain visible.
scope: Hot-initialized boundary replay of ContinuousPlant.thermal (ColdStartPlant), not a run of the continuous cold-start trajectory. Measured core heat and secondary flows exclude kinetics and turbine/generator/controller validation.

protocol.purpose: Evaluate the exact thermal kernel composed by ContinuousPlant against a previously available measured plant event. This is a development comparison, not a blind validation data set.
protocol.initialPointPolicy: Table 2 initializes the model; interpolated measured t=0 is displayed only to expose initialization bias and is excluded from error metrics.
protocol.numericalLimitMeaning: Conservation quadrature and step-refinement checks only; never physical prediction-error acceptance.
protocol.parameterPolicy: Use published initial conditions and nominal pump heat, disclosed generic capacities and volumes, and initial-only balance-derived conductances and enthalpies. Do not tune parameters using any post-initialization response.
protocol.domainStopPolicy: Preserve a failed sensitivity's finite terminal observation and mark it failed-domain. Never extrapolate it, call it a completed pass, change the parameter to avoid its failure, or report a full-window spread for an incomplete pair. Mandatory nominal/refined domain exits fail execution and block publication.
protocol.referencePolicy: Use original acquired measured curves, not RELAP5 cal curves; preserve immutable input bytes and existing channel assignments. Missing event-era geometry, actuator histories, level-to-volume mappings and instrument uncertainty prevent physical acceptance.

experiment.plant: Krško, Westinghouse two-loop PWR, post-2000 uprate, core cycle 21

eventDateResolution.reportConflict: NUREG/IA-0221 abstract (PDF page 5), introduction (printed page 1) and conclusion (printed page 55) say 10 April; the event-description paragraph on printed page 9 says 5 April.
eventDateResolution.independentSource: NEK Annual Report 2005, PDF page 13, Operational events: 10 April 2005 turbine-valve test followed by SI and trip. The separate condenser-vacuum event is dated 11 April.
eventDateResolution.effectOnTimeSeries: None. Relative time convention and original numeric channels are unchanged.

experiment.eventTimeConvention: Report section 4: t=0 is the inferred start of governor-valve closure, 53 seconds after the source acquisition began.
experiment.windowRationale: End before operator reopening at approximately 16 s and inferred SI/reactor trip at approximately 17 s. The report warns that post-trip neutron-power and flow indications do not directly represent total decay heat and actual flows; those intervals are excluded.
experiment.measurementTimingAllowanceBasis: Half of the reported 2 s acquisition interval; a comparison allowance, not a quantified instrument-delay distribution.

extraction.method: Read PDF vector vertices of the magenta measured instrument curve in panel (a); exclude blue curves labeled cal and all legend symbols.
extraction.timeRounding: Vector x-coordinates match -49,-47,...,49 s within 0.06 s. They are snapped to that stated acquisition grid; values are rounded to six decimals for reproducibility, not six-digit measurement accuracy.
extraction.readingAllowance: A conservative half-PDF-point vertical reading allowance is recorded per channel by the extractor. It is roughly 0.006 MPa for primary pressure, 0.005 MPa for SG pressure, 0.04 K for cold legs and 0.13 K for hot legs. It covers figure extraction only, not instrument uncertainty.
extraction.pressureAxisCorrection: Figures 29,33,34 label pressure in MPa but print bar-valued ticks (primary 144–162; SG 64–80). Multiply these tick values by 0.1 to recover MPa. This is corroborated independently by measured Table 2 initial pressure 15.48 MPa and SG pressures 6.42/6.40 MPa; raw printed values must not be treated as 154.8 MPa or 64.2 MPa.
extraction.additionalControls: chargingFlowLS (AF00793_FT205, Figure 31) and letdownFlowLS (AF00795_FT132, Figure 32) retain the source litres/second unit. Their highest labelled horizontal gridline is 8 L/s; the vertical axis extends above it, so the extractor uses the labelled gridline rather than the unlabelled endpoint. No density, reference-temperature, pressure, or incoming-enthalpy conversion is invented.
extraction.additionalResponse: pressurizerLevelPercent (AL00818_LT465, Figure 30) is an indicated level with a 0–70 percent plotted scale. It is not a measured liquid-volume fraction; geometry and level-instrument transfer functions are required for that interpretation.
extraction.aggregation: Hot/cold temperatures and SG pressures are unweighted means of the two reported loop instruments. Steam and feedwater flows are sums. These means do not resolve loop asymmetry.
extraction.powerConversion: Before trip, reported neutron power percent multiplied by 1994 MW / 100. It is a thermal-input proxy, not direct calorimetry and not a valid post-trip decay-heat measurement.

initialConditions.basis: Measured t=0 column of Table 2 (printed page 13, PDF page 25), with arithmetic means for two-loop temperatures and pressure.

calibrationAndHoldout.initializationData: Only Table 2 initial values calibrate the nominal heat-transfer conductances and feedwater enthalpy needed for constructed equilibrium.
calibrationAndHoldout.parameterFitting: No transient response channel is used to fit volumes, heat capacities, conductances, control gains or time constants. No optimization is performed.
calibrationAndHoldout.acceptance: No plant-validation acceptance band is asserted: the source does not supply instrument uncertainties or the complete plant geometry/input deck needed for this reduced model. Errors are reported even when large. Numerical success does not turn the applicability assessment into a validation pass.

limitations: This is a short, boundary-driven thermal/inventory comparison. Measured core power and secondary flows are inputs, so the test does not validate neutron kinetics, turbine controls, generator, feedwater controls or trip logic.

The primary hot/cold volumes, fuel heat capacity, pressurizer volume, and secondary volume remain generic assumptions scaled from OpenPWR by initial core thermal power/3000 MW. They are not identified Krško geometry.
A homogeneous equilibrium secondary model omits distributed boiling, subcooled feedwater mixing, SG walls and instrument shrink/swell. The primary model omits wall heat storage and transport delays.

Initial feedwater enthalpy is inferred from a zero initial secondary energy-rate balance because inlet enthalpy is not given in the selected report. The measured feedwater/steam mismatch is retained, so initial secondary mass inventory need not be exactly stationary.
The v0.5 replay omitted pump heat. The current case applies the documented nominal 6 MW as a separate constant boundary, not as a measured time history or fitted parameter.

The v0.5 replay fixed heater, spray, charging and letdown to zero. Measured charging/letdown curves in litres per second are now included, but instrument reference conditions and incoming-water enthalpy remain unestablished. Heater and spray numerical histories are unavailable in the reviewed event sources; their omission or assumed reconstruction limits pressure interpretation.

The pre-event figure curves indicate aggregate steam flow around 1003 kg/s and feedwater around 996 kg/s, while Table 2 lists roughly the reverse. Instrument identifiers in Table 3 and captions are followed without swapping, offsetting or fitting the curves. The inconsistency remains a source-input limitation.
Instrument calibration accuracy and delay distributions are unavailable; graphical reading allowances cannot replace them.
The published curves are a rendered representation of measurements, not the original raw acquisition dataset.

genericGeometry.primaryVolumeM3: 300 * referenceScale * geometryScale; production kernel allocates equal hot and cold halves
genericGeometry.status: Unidentified event-era allocations; generic dimensions inherited from the existing replay. These are not Krško plant measurements. The 0.5 and 2 multipliers are uncalibrated sensitivities.

initialBalanceDerived.qualification: Initial-only energy-rate constructions, not independently measured flow, material properties or conductance. The curve/table mismatch and mass imbalance prevent asserting a complete measured steady state.

parameterSources.initialGasAssumption: Pressurizer and secondary temperature equal the IF97 saturation temperature at the published initial pressure, with zero noncondensable cover-gas inventory. No plant nitrogen inventory was measured in this event.

omittedControls.spray: The shared cold-start thermal kernel has no spray port. No numeric spray history is supplied; the event report describes spray action qualitatively. This missing actuator is a pressure-prediction limitation, not a validated zero-flow observation.
omittedControls.chargingLetdown: Measured L/s are retained in the original CSV but not converted without reference density, instrument location and inlet enthalpy.
omittedControls.ventShutdownCooling: Closed/disabled for this hot 15 s boundary replay; native equations remain unchanged.
omittedControls.automaticControls: Pressure and inventory controllers disabled; imposed external heat and secondary flows exclude production reactor/cycle controls from this comparison.

parameterSources.scope: The reference wrapper composes the same ColdStartPlant class used by ContinuousPlant. It does not execute the ContinuousPlant reactor, turbine, condenser or electrical subsystems, and it does not test the cold startup trajectory.

sourceLedger.purpose: Separate published facts from usable 2005 model parameters, unresolved boundaries, and rejected substitutions. No value is inferred by fitting measured pressure or temperature.
